The previously reviewed construction changes only the zero and one fibers in the all-zero binary layer. The first-coordinate-one fiber in that layer is the only changed fiber with first coordinate one, so its share is precisely Δ_1/(Δ_0+Δ_1). Both revised sentences now identify that share explicitly.
The planar area and perimeter calculation is unchanged. For every t>0, the area increment Δ_0 is positive and Steiner scaling gives Δ_1=(3/4)Δ_0. Exact fraction arithmetic gives (3/4)/(1+3/4)=3/7.

The lower bound 1/(2^d+1) on the total fraction at distance at least one and the weak nonconvergence assertion are unchanged. The revised exact identity only counts the base-one fiber, so it is consistent with large bumps for which some base-zero addition is also at distance greater than one.

Reconfirmed the retained n≥1, d≥2, t>0 scope, the Brunn–Minkowski and containment bounds, the locality at base zero, and the unchanged small-bump threshold Δ_0<V/4. The quantitative statements and the source locators §5–§5.2, (14)–(19) are unchanged.

The displayed linear functional has value one only at (0,e_1) on the original cylinder. At any base whose binary coordinate is one, all components of a representing combination have that coordinate one, excluding the apex. At the all-zero layer all components must have those coordinates zero. Grouping by the first-coordinate endpoints gives the exact interpolated fiber; the interpolation contains the original B_d at every first coordinate.

Brunn–Minkowski and the binomial expansion give Δ_1/V≥Δ_0/(2^d V) since the highest term increases by exactly x/2^d and all other increases are nonnegative. Convexity and B_d⊂K(t) give Δ_1≤Δ_0. Only the zero and one fibers gain mass, so the base-one share is at least 1/(2^d+1). A bounded continuous test zero near w and one on the set at distance at least one rules out a point-mass weak limit.
On the base-zero addition the separator ν has ν·y>1, with (1+t)ν·e_1>1 and ||y||≤1+t. Thus ||y−ν||²<(1+t)²−1 and ||ν−e_1||²<2t/(1+t), proving uniform locality.

The tangent points in the plane are (1/a, ±s/a) by orthogonality of the tangents and radii. Direct cap-area subtraction gives s³/a² + s/a² − θ = s−θ since s²+1=a². The perimeter replaces arc length 2θ by segments of total length 2s. The parallel-body area is 4π+3Δ_0, and area scales by 1/4 at factor 1/2. Therefore Δ_1=3Δ_0/4 and its fraction is exactly 3/7 for every t>0.

The count of original fibers is 3·2^(n−1), yielding original threshold 3V/2. The perturbed total is at least the original, while each new fiber has mass at most V+Δ_0<5V/4 under the stated assumption.
